source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS01 is the third-largest data center in Virginia by disclosed capacity, at 114 MW across 685,000 square feet.

The facility accounts for 7.1 percent of the 1,603 MW published by Virginia's 25 disclosing facilities. That concentration matters because AI training clusters are sized in tens of megawatts, and a single campus at this scale can absorb a meaningful share of what a regional grid makes available. At 40 kW per rack, the published capacity implies roughly 2,850 racks, though the operator does not state the workload mix or tenant configuration.

The gap is the story. Virginia has 330 mapped facilities, and only 25 publish megawatt figures. The rest are invisible to any public accounting of how much load the state's grid is actually carrying. LEED certification speaks to building efficiency, not to where the power comes from or how it reaches the site.

What this record does not contain is the part that determines whether the campus constrains AI scaling: its power source, its grid connection point, and whether the 114 MW is allocated or available. Without those, the capacity figure describes a building, not a load.
